before.title: A/C Compressor Clutch Failure
before.description: The Murano A/C compressor clutch is prone to failure, particularly on the first and second generation models. The clutch relay, clutch coil, or the compressor clutch bearing can fail, resulting in no A/C cooling. Symptoms often start with intermittent A/C operation — cooling works sometimes but not others — before progressing to complete failure. A seized compressor clutch bearing will produce a constant squealing noise with the A/C off.
before.solution: If only the clutch coil has failed, it can be replaced separately ($100-200 parts + $150-250 labor). If the clutch bearing is seized, the compressor assembly typically needs replacement ($400-800 for aftermarket compressor, $300-500 labor). The system needs to be evacuated and recharged ($100-150). Replace the receiver drier when replacing the compressor.
symptoms: A/C blows warm air intermittently
A/C stops cooling completely
Squealing noise from engine bay
A/C clutch not engaging
Burning rubber smell with A/C on

communityRecommendations.text: Check the A/C relay first ($15 part) before assuming the compressor is bad - it fails frequently on Muranos

before.title: Automatic Emergency Braking / Forward Collision Phantom Activation
before.description: Third-generation Muranos with Nissan's Forward Emergency Braking (FEB)/Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) have widely reported 'phantom braking' — the system suddenly and forcefully brakes when no obstacle is present, creating rear-end collision and loss-of-control risk. The problem is associated with the front grille radar/sensor module (Bosch-supplied) misreading the road. The Murano is named in AEB class-action litigation alongside other Nissan models, and Nissan issued TSBs addressing false AEB/FCW activation on 2019-2024 Murano (Z52).
before.solution: Dealer diagnosis per the applicable TSB; remedies have included radar sensor recalibration, software/ECU reprogramming, or sensor replacement. Keep the front emblem/grille radar area clean and free of obstructions (snow, mud, badges). The FEB system can be temporarily disabled via the vehicle settings menu while driving in conditions that trigger false activation.
symptoms: Sudden hard braking with no obstacle present
Phantom deceleration on open road
Forward collision warning with nothing ahead
Unintended braking near overpasses or oncoming cars

before.title: AWD Transfer Case Failure / Fluid Leak (2nd Gen)
before.description: Second-generation AWD Muranos have a known transfer case defect, referenced in Nissan service bulletin NTB17-003, where the transfer case leaks fluid and fails. The unit cannot be repaired and must be replaced, with dealer replacement commonly around $3,000-$3,500. Owners report that an unaddressed failing transfer case can produce whining/clunking noises and, in severe cases, lock up the driveline at highway speeds.
before.solution: Diagnose early at the first sign of leaking or noise; the transfer case is replaced as a unit (it is not serviceable internally). Keeping the AWD coupling/transfer case fluid changed on schedule helps. Verify the rear-diff/coupling and driveshaft after replacement.
symptoms: Transfer case fluid leak
Whining or growling from the driveline
Clunking under acceleration or load
AWD warning / driveline lockup at speed

before.title: Battery Drain and No-Start from Telematics/Infotainment Modules Staying Awake
before.description: A recurring owner complaint on newer Nissan crossovers, including Murano, is a dead battery after sitting overnight or for a few days despite the battery testing good initially. Reports often point to parasitic draw from telematics, AV control, or body control modules that fail to enter sleep mode, sometimes accompanied by app connectivity glitches or infotainment oddities. The issue can be intermittent, making it difficult to catch unless a proper draw test is performed after module timeout.
before.solution: Start with battery state-of-health and charging-system checks, then perform a parasitic draw test with the vehicle fully asleep. If draw remains excessive, isolate the circuit by pulling fuses and checking telematics, AV, and BCM-related branches; software updates, module resets, or replacement of the offending module may be required. Replacing the battery alone often provides only temporary relief if the root draw remains.
symptoms: dead battery after sitting
slow cranking or no-start
needs jump start repeatedly
battery tests weak prematurely
infotainment or NissanConnect glitches

citations.title: Murano forum discussions on repeated dead battery and parasitic draw

communityRecommendations.content: Ask for a true parasitic draw test after all modules time out; many quick battery tests miss the actual problem.
If the vehicle sits for long periods, a smart maintainer can prevent deep discharge while diagnosis is pending.

before.title: Premature Catalytic Converter Failure
before.description: The Murano VQ35DE is prone to premature catalytic converter failure, often between 80,000-120,000 miles. The Bank 1 (firewall side) converter typically fails first. Contributing factors include the engine's tendency toward oil consumption, which poisons the catalyst, and heat soak from the converter's close proximity to the engine. Failed converters trigger emission codes and can cause reduced power and failed emissions tests.
before.solution: Replace the failed catalytic converter(s). OEM converters are very expensive ($1,500-2,500 each). Quality aftermarket CARB-compliant converters cost $400-800. Address any oil consumption issues before or during converter replacement to prevent repeat failure. Walker, Eastern Catalytic, and MagnaFlow make reliable aftermarket replacements.
symptoms: Check engine light with P0420/P0430
Rotten egg or sulfur smell
Reduced engine power
Failed emissions test
Rattling noise from under hood

before.title: CVT Transmission Judder, Slipping, and Premature Failure
before.description: Third-generation Muranos equipped with Nissan's JATCO continuously variable transmission (CVT) commonly develop juddering/shuddering on light acceleration, hesitation, lag, overheating, and outright failure, frequently before 100,000 miles. Nissan acknowledged the judder via TSB and stored DTCs P17F0/P17F1, and a class-action settlement (Beaver v. Nissan North America) extended the CVT warranty to 84 months/84,000 miles for 2015-2018 Muranos with up to $5,000 in repair reimbursement. Earlier 2003-2010 CVT-equipped models also suffered widespread slipping and failure. Full replacement commonly runs $4,000-$8,000.
before.solution: Under the extended warranty (84 mo/84k mi for 2015-2018), have the dealer diagnose the stored code: P17F1 typically calls for CVT valve-body/sub-assembly replacement while P17F0 requires full transmission replacement. Keep CVT fluid (Nissan NS-3) changed on a shortened interval (~30k miles) and consider an auxiliary CVT cooler to reduce overheating. Out of warranty, a remanufactured CVT or valve body is the fix.
symptoms: Shuddering or juddering on light acceleration
Hesitation or delayed engagement
Slipping or RPM flare without acceleration
Loss of power / failure to launch from a stop
Whining noise
Transmission overheating
Limp mode

before.title: Front Driver Seat Frame/Track Looseness Causing Rocking, Clicking, or Unintended Movement
before.description: Owners have reported the driver's seat rocking front-to-back, clicking during braking/acceleration, or feeling loose on its track. Nissan has issued service information on seat track/frame-related movement complaints on late-model vehicles, and owner reports indicate the issue can appear at relatively low mileage. The problem is usually caused by play in the seat track assembly, frame hardware, or worn internal seat adjuster components rather than the floor mounting points themselves.
before.solution: Road-test the vehicle and confirm whether the movement occurs during throttle tip-in, braking, or over bumps. Inspect seat track bolts, rail alignment, and the seat adjuster assembly; repairs typically involve tightening hardware to spec, replacing the seat track/adjuster assembly, or replacing the seat frame if internal play is present. If the seat has power functions, verify all positions after repair and recalibrate memory settings if equipped.
symptoms: driver seat rocks during braking
clicking from seat base
seat shifts slightly on acceleration
loose feeling in seat track
movement felt through seat cushion

citations.title: Murano owner forum discussions on driver seat rocking/clicking

communityRecommendations.content: Have the dealer verify torque on seat mounting fasteners before replacing expensive seat components.
Document exactly when the seat moves—braking, acceleration, or cornering—to help isolate track vs. frame play.

before.title: Front Radar/Sensor Malfunctions Triggering AEB, ICC, and Forward Collision Warnings
before.description: Owners have reported intermittent 'Front radar unavailable,' AEB/FCW warnings, disabled intelligent cruise control, and related driver-assistance faults on 2021-2024 Murano models. In many cases the system disables itself in rain, road spray, or after minor front-end impacts, but some complaints describe repeated warnings in normal conditions due to sensor alignment, bracket movement, contamination, or radar unit faults. Because these systems are tied to emergency braking and adaptive cruise functions, repeated failures are a significant safety concern.
before.solution: Scan all ADAS modules for stored faults and inspect the front radar sensor area for damage, contamination, or mounting/bracket misalignment. Nissan service procedures typically require radar aiming/calibration after bumper work or sensor replacement; if warnings persist, the radar sensor, harness, or bracket may need replacement followed by static/dynamic calibration. Also verify battery voltage and CAN communication health, since low voltage can trigger cascading ADAS faults.
symptoms: front radar unavailable message
AEB warning light
forward collision warning disabled
intelligent cruise control unavailable
intermittent ADAS warnings in clear weather

citations.title: Murano owner forum discussions on front radar unavailable / ICC disabled

communityRecommendations.content: Do not replace the radar blindly; first inspect the emblem area, bracket, and bumper fitment, then perform proper calibration.

before.title: VQ35DE 3.5L Excessive Oil Consumption
before.description: The first-generation Murano's VQ35DE 3.5L V6 is known for high oil consumption as it ages, often well before 100,000 miles. Owners report burning roughly a quart every 1,000-2,500 miles (worse in some cases). The cause is attributed to piston ring sealing problems against slightly tapered cylinder bores, producing blow-by; some owners also report oil pooling in the intake/PCV hoses. Left unchecked, low oil accelerates timing chain and bearing wear.
before.solution: Monitor oil level frequently and top up between changes; replace/clean the PCV valve and oil-fouled hoses. Verified repairs include updated piston ring sets (an engine re-ring) or, in severe cases, engine replacement — both costly. Using the correct oil grade/viscosity and shorter change intervals slows consumption.
symptoms: Frequent need to add oil between changes
Low oil level / oil light
Burning oil smell
Blue exhaust smoke on startup or acceleration
Oil in intake/PCV hoses

proposal.title: VQ35DE 3.5L Excessive Oil Consumption
proposal.description: The complete exact Murano communication and recall corpus does not establish excessive VQ35DE oil consumption across 2003-2007, PCV oil ingestion, piston-ring wear or catalyst damage as one first-generation defect. Owner complaints and generic engine summaries can describe experiences but do not prove a manufacturer-defined consumption rate, common mechanism or affected population.
proposal.solution: Document oil level and distance with a controlled consumption test, inspect external leaks and service history, and evaluate PCV operation, intake oil, compression, leak-down, smoke, plugs and catalyst DTCs before naming a cause. Do not buy a PCV valve, rings, additives, engine or converter from this page; measured rate, root cause, oil specification and VIN fitment must be established first.
symptoms: oil level and distance documented under a controlled test
external leakage and service history checked
PCV, ring, valve-seal and combustion paths separated
